## dcim_connected-device_list

<a id="opIddcim_connected-device_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/dcim/connected-device/?peer_device=string&peer_interface=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /dcim/connected-device/`

This endpoint allows a user to determine what device (if any) is connected to a given peer device and peer
interface. This is useful in a situation where a device boots with no configuration, but can detect its neighbors
via a protocol such as LLDP. Two query parameters must be included in the request:

* `peer_device`: The name of the peer device
* `peer_interface`: The name of the peer interface

<h3 id="dcimconnected-devicelist-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|peer_device|query|string|true|The name of the peer device|
|peer_interface|query|string|true|The name of the peer interface|

## dcim_interfaces_delete

<a id="opIddcim_interfaces_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/dcim/interfaces/0/ \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /dcim/interfaces/{id}/`

<h3 id="dciminterfacesdelete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|integer|true|A unique integer value identifying this interface.|

<h3 id="dciminterfacesdelete-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content||None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Bearer
</aside>

|» type|body|string|false|The type of data this custom field holds|
|» ui_visibility|body|string|false|Specifies the visibility of custom field in the UI|
|» validation_maximum|body|integer \| null|false|Maximum allowed value (for numeric fields)|
|» validation_minimum|body|integer \| null|false|Minimum allowed value (for numeric fields)|
|» validation_regex|body|string|false|Regular expression to enforce on text field values. Use ^ and $ to force matching of entire string. For example, <code>^[A-Z]{3}$</code> will limit values to exactly three uppercase letters.|
|» weight|body|integer|false|Fields with higher weights appear lower in a form.|
